rows.claim: Staging cells and the published reference are release/acquire @atomic fields
rows.evidence: src/dataplane.jl:26 (`@atomic pending`, default ordering); src/dataplane.jl:492 (`@atomicswap`, default); src/dataplane.jl:465 (`@atomicreplace`, default); src/sim.jl:2797 (release-store), src/sim.jl:2857 (acquire-load)
rows.fix: Say the published reference is stored with release and loaded with acquire, and the staging cell's operations (`@atomicreplace` merge, `@atomicswap` take, `@atomic` load) use Julia's default sequentially consistent ordering, which is stronger. Or: 'single words, `@atomic` fields, the published reference with release/acquire ordering'.
rows.note: Only the published reference and the heartbeat/flag fields name :release/:acquire. Soundness is unaffected since seq_cst implies release/acquire.

rows.claim: Pre-materializing activations leaves no worker synchronizing on anything
rows.evidence: src/build.jl:970-974 (`activation` takes `@lock build.lock` on every lookup, hit included); src/build.jl:708
rows.fix: Replace 'leaves no worker synchronizing on anything' with 'leaves every activation lookup a hit under the build's short lock, with no first-request race and no re-derivation'. Or, as a defect, make the hit path lock-free (read the dictionary without the lock once all activations are materialized).
rows.note: Same overstatement at spec.md:5750 ('no synchronization on any path'), outside this slice. Each Simulation constructs one activation lookup, so the lock is brief and uncontended in practice.

rows.claim: Attach refuses a binding whose read fails with the read's own kind, ReadResolution

rows.fix: Attach refuses such a binding with the read's own kind, `ReadResolution`, or `PathResolution` where a path names no component (D-440), every violation collected in one throw.
